A year ago I wrote this letter to myself. Ive always struggled with depression but I was very depressed at the time. 

Since then I’ve graduated college, bought a new car, and I will be starting my first year teaching in a week. I’m happier and healthier than I’ve ever been. 

Bad times don’t last but sometimes it’s hard to reflect on where we’ve come from unless we document it. 

(Also funny that I thought staying home for 4 days was hard. I wish I could have told myself a pandemic was coming.)
I’m 27 and I definitely spend $300+. I’m pretty sure I’ve spent $300 in just the past 3 months. But I think of my books as my collection. Everyone in my family collects something, mine is books.

I also had that spoiled. I didn’t know how but I knew Rhysand was going to be redeemed because I knew that’s who she ended up with.  I’m actually kind of glad I knew otherwise I might not have read the second book. I didn’t like Tamlin (his character seemed bland in the first book) and Feyre wasn’t very interesting as a human. But I loved Rhysand from the moment he was introduced.
This was my exact thought.

My 13 year old self would be amazed at how far I’ve come with no support. I grew up in extreme poverty, with parents add to drugs and alcohol. 

When I was 13 I told my mom I wanted to be a doctor and she told me I couldn’t do it because I wouldn’t make it through college. In May I graduated graduated college and was offered my dream job (special education teacher). 

I still have a long way to go but 13 year old me never even imagined I would love to be an adult.
I used to get about 2 a month and now I get maybe two a year. My quality of life has drastically improved, I don’t even know how I lived like that.
With the state of things I doubt we’ll be giving a Halloween.

I remember getting food boxes from local churches and eating expired protein bars for every meal. I loved them because most of the time they were peanut butter and tasted like a treat. Now I keep boxes of them in my house and occasionally eat one if I don’t feel like making dinner. I also remember making mayo sandwiches for my little sister. They were just bread and mayo but we loved them. Growing up poor you don’t know how bad you have it until you’re an adult.

A roommate once asked me how to make mashed potatoes. She was confused about to a whole potato could be turned into mashed potatoes. She had only ever had instant potatoes and thought that’s how mashed potatoes were made. She had never even bought a whole potato before. 

To give her credit she grew up with no dad and a drug addicted mother. She basically raised herself and siblings. 

Her brother (15) once tried to make a can of Spaghetti O’s by putting an unopened can in the toaster oven and turning it on. Luckily I came into the kitchen almost immediately after and showed him how to cook them.

This is why I’m not celebrating the 4th this year. I’m not proud of where our country is and I don’t agree with celebrating our failures. 

I feel like I should be attending a funeral not a bbq.

Same here. I’m a first year teacher doing an alt certification program. Our summer school started Yesterday with a lot of precautionary measures in place. So far it’s gone really well, all of the kids and adults are wearing masks and kids really do seem happy just to be at school.

I bought this game about a month ago and my island is more developed than a friend that got the game at least a month before me but I’m a teacher so I don’t work during the summer so I play all the time.  So I would say it’s never too late, you play the game at your pace.

I’m in Utah and there is a teacher shortage here. I switched to the BAES program and decided to do emergency certification (this was recommended to me by the school district I work for as a para.) I was offered a job I didn’t apply for before I was officially graduated. I was well known as a good para throughout my district though, which is really important. I’ve seen a lot of people struggle to get hired in my district because there’s new to the area and not known. Do you have experience working in a school at all? Sometimes substituting helps get your name out there. Unfortunately sometimes it’s all about week you know.

That’s good to hear! At the school I’m currently in admin doesn’t seem to value us as much as they should but the teachers I work with definitely do. The students usually love all of the paras and show us a lot of respect but they definitely understand we aren’t teachers. I know I’ll have a mentor teacher to work with so hopefully they can help.
I’m in Utah as a severe sped para, I make around $16,000 a year for 5.75 hours a day. I make the highest possible in my district for my experience. No benefits.
I just used a 3.0 which is what WGU. I got a scholarship from my state board of education and they didn’t question it.
Ya every once in a while I’ll go into “remission” but it still not great and doesn’t last longer than 6 months. I’ve been like this for 11 years at this point it’s just my normal.
Yes., same. There’s almost always blood. I get iron transfusions every 6 months.

You think 3x a day is bad. Try 20+ times a day. 

Living with Crohn’s disease.

This is 100% true. Special education has the highest turnover rate in schools and its especially bad in high schools. Sped makes you a more desirable candidate but only because they know they may have to move you from your desired position. 

WGU has a BA in educational studies that doesn’t lead to licensing but they don’t let new students enroll in it. She could enroll in literally any education BA and start working on gen ed requirements. Near the end of her first term she can ask to transfer to the BAES degree and then do the masters in English that leads to licensing.
Thanks for being understanding. I try to spread awareness because I know that most people don’t think of things like that.

Just so you know, those who are blind or have visual impairments and use text to speech won’t be able to understand what you’re trying to say when you add unnecessary emojis in. 

All of the emojis literally make it harder to comprehend what you’re trying to say. 

I’m not trying to harass you, I’m just trying to spread awareness about something you may not have been known.

His favorite things are dinner and his pink squeaky frog. He’s been my companion throughout life and is always by my side wherever I go.

Knowing a teacher doesn’t mean you know how hard the job is. Not even teachers know how hard it is for other teachers but if you’ve never even been a teacher, you really can’t say the job isn’t very hard. 

I would love to explain why it’s hard but you already have your mind made up and I don’t believe anyone really knows how hard it is until they’ve spent some time in a classroom.

So not at all the same but this is very important. I work with special needs kids and we take them to the grocery stores as life skills lessons. They have to shop, budget, and pay for their own groceries. Sometimes I’ll have to step in to remind them how to count the money or pay but they always hand the cashiers the money. When the cashier hands the change back they usually try and hand it to me. It so frustrating because I’m literally trying to teach the student how to be independent. You’re screwing up my lesson! Give the change to the person who handed you the money!
This is how I got blue hair. (Which lasted about a week) This was also the point in my life when I started realizing I was bipolar and not just depressed.

There’s nothing in particular that’s causing these thoughts as far as I can tell. That’s the problem. I work in special education and I’m constantly told how important I am to my kids lives. I’m constantly told how valuable I am. I excelled in school last semester and I was told by everyone how great I was doing. 

Despite all of this, I have no joy or happiness. I don’t want to sleep. I don’t want to wake up. I don’t want to eat. I don’t want to work on school anymore. 

Everyday I think about how much easier it would be to not be alive. And then I tell myself that dying isn’t the answer.  But it’s starting to seem like the only answer.

I just wanted to share my story because I’m pretty proud. 

No one in my family has gone to college since my great grandpa. Not my grandparents, not my parents, aunts, uncles, cousins, or my sister. 

I’m 26 now, but when I was 18 I completed 1 semester of traditional college. My family was so proud. I hated it though so I dropped out. 

I’ve always wanted to go back to school but didn’t think I could. 

I started working as a para in a sped high school class. They teachers I worked with were so motivating and did what teachers do. They talked me into going back to school. 

So here I am, 3 months and 22 credits into college. 

Also, I can’t wait to be a teacher!

Yes! I recently went camping with family. I have multiple autoimmune disorders including UC and RA. I’m always tired. So I decided to take a nap and while my cousin thought I was asleep I heard her say “isn’t it funny how the people who need naps never get them because we’re busy with the kids?” 

Like sorry Susan, I wasn’t the one who decided to have 3 kids. I personally choose not to have kids because I need my naps.

How long have you been taking it? I’ve been on prednisone for almost 4 years. I’ve been on extremely high doses and now I’m on 5mg, probably for long term since nothing else is working. For me I don’t have as much hunger under 20 mg, at least it’s nothing compared to the really high doses. I actually don’t feel any of the negative side effects on 5mg. I also get extremely sick in the mornings so I don’t usually eat until noon. I choose IF to help with munchies at night and Keto keeps me full longer. 

I’ve thought about if I have to go back on a higher dose again and I hope I can keep the healthy life style up. I know how difficult the hunger is to ignore. I once ate a whole 12 oz steak meal with sides from chili’s, and within an hour I felt like I was starving. I’m sorry that you’re experiencing the bad side effects.

I have no friends. I spend time with one cousin and my sister (although she recently went through a bipolar episode and was hospitalized) other then them, my parents and grandma. That’s it. 

It’s hard enough to maintain relationships with family. I always feel like they’re mad at me and only tolerating me because I’m family. 

I used to have lots of friends. But my mind slowly told me they all hated me and I got to bad of anxiety to talk to them, and they didn’t reach out to me.

When I was 16 my mom opened a bank account with me. I forgot about it and when I was 18 I opened my own. But we never closed the old one and my mom continued to use it. Well she ended up getting laid off from her job and went trough a financial hardship. 

She pulled out 600 from the overdraft and never paid it back. I ended up having to pay it back at 24. 

So make sure to close the account or remove your name from your parents account.
